verdicts.summary: The note's only real hazard is the one finding 0 already reports. When the first Connect call fails, the footer has no code-fallback link, because `environment` is set only after a call succeeds.
Peer-link clients are kept on the environment's own page, and other hosts fall back to `/connect-agent`.
verdicts.scenario: A peer-link client calls /authorize on the linked tunnel host. The handler skips `hostedApprovalUrl` and redirects to `/connect-agent`. A crafted hosted link for a peer-link client reaches the same `approve()`, and that path already allowed browser-session decisions before this change.

verdicts.summary: A timed-out decision POST, which the server may already have applied, is shown as an 'unreachable with this account' error. Finding 1 already covers this. Retrying mints a new single-use code and redirects, so the retry itself is harmless.
The client's redirect filter accepts at least every redirect the server can produce.
verdicts.scenario: Agent registered `http://[::1]:5555/cb`. On the server, `URL.hostname` is `[::1]`, which is in `LOOPBACK_HOSTNAMES`. On the client, `isLoopbackHost` accepts `[::1]`, localhost and 127.0.0.1. Error redirects go through `redirectWith`, which builds them on the registered redirect URI, so they are absolute https or loopback-http URLs and are never refused.

verdicts.summary: The Approve delay re-arms on every focus or visibility change and is cleaned up on unmount. Enter-to-submit goes through the same `canApprove` check.
verdicts.scenario: The page reaches ready and the user switches tabs twice quickly. Each `rearm` clears the previous timer and starts a new one, so Approve becomes enabled 700 ms after the last event. The status never leaves ready, so the effect does not tear down partway through.

verdicts.summary: The note's open question is the one finding 6 asks: does the server refuse a session approval under a `remoteClients` policy? `approve()` and `approvingSession` do not check managed policy. Server code checks `allowsRemoteClients` only when it creates pairing links, so whether this path is refused depends on the relay session being refused.

Every failure is mapped to ConnectMcpApprovalUnavailableError, which leaves the other message branch in ApproveAgentSurface unreachable. Finding 1 already covers this. A stale token on the decision call comes back as a typed AuthMcpApprovalError and is never renewed, which is the session-renewal problem finding 2 raises.
